stem: A kidney waitlist candidate is placed on inactive status while temporarily unsuitable for transplant. According to OPTN Policy 3.6.A, how does waiting time accrue during inactivity?

options.text: Waiting time accrues without limit while the candidate remains inactive
No waiting time accrues for any kidney candidate while inactive
Waiting time accrues only for the first 30 cumulative inactive days
Waiting time resets to zero whenever inactive status is assigned

explanation.rationale_correct: OPTN Table 3-3 specifies that kidney candidates accrue unlimited waiting time while inactive, although inactive candidates do not receive organ offers.

rationale_incorrect.B: Heart candidates do not accrue waiting time while inactive, but kidney candidates accrue unlimited time.
rationale_incorrect.C: A 30-day cumulative limit applies to intestine candidates, not kidney candidates.
rationale_incorrect.D: Kidney waiting time continues to accrue during inactive periods rather than resetting to zero.

primary_anchor.section: Policy 3.6.A → Table 3-3 Waiting Time for Inactive Candidates → Kidney
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Kidney … Unlimited time … Candidates accrue waiting time while inactive

references.locator: Policy 3.6.A → Table 3-3: Waiting Time for Inactive Candidates (kidney candidates accrue unlimited waiting time while inactive); PDF p. 46 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 020500 item; kidney inactive waiting-time accrual distinct from no-offers (cctc-2012) and inactive-reason (cctc-2005); anchor verified on optn-policies p. 46.

stem: A candidate with type 1 diabetes and progressive renal insufficiency completes multidisciplinary evaluation. For which transplant option is simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplantation MOST appropriate?

options.text: Diabetes with renal insufficiency meeting SPK selection criteria
Isolated end-stage renal disease without diabetes
Stable type 2 diabetes with normal renal function only

explanation.rationale_correct: Simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplantation is indicated for candidates with diabetes or pancreatic exocrine insufficiency together with renal insufficiency.

rationale_incorrect.B: Isolated ESRD without diabetes is an indication for kidney transplant alone, not SPK.
rationale_incorrect.C: SPK requires renal insufficiency in addition to diabetes; normal renal function alone does not indicate SPK.
rationale_incorrect.D: Primary biliary cirrhosis without diabetes is a liver transplant indication, not SPK.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 15, Pancreas Transplantation → B. Simultaneous pancreas-kidney (SPK) → 1.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Diagnosis of diabetes or pancreatic exocrine insufficiency with renal insufficiency

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 15 → B. Simultaneous pancreas-kidney (SPK) transplantation → 1. (diabetes with renal insufficiency); PDF p. 825 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 020300 item; second kidney_pancreas organ tag; SPK suitability distinct from pancreas-alone approval (cctc-2029); anchor verified on Cupples p. 825.

stem: When presenting deceased-donor organ offer information to a transplant physician team, which donor detail must be disclosed to the recipient if it is critical to informed consent?

options.text: Unrelated donor employment history with no clinical relevance
The procurement coordinator's personal contact list

explanation.rationale_correct: Recipients may be informed of specific donor information critical to informed consent, including possible donor-transmitted disease risks and organ characteristics that could affect function.

rationale_incorrect.B: Donor family vacation plans are not clinically relevant donor information for transplant consent.
rationale_incorrect.C: Unrelated employment history without clinical relevance is not required donor disclosure.
rationale_incorrect.D: Staff personal contact information is not part of donor-offer clinical disclosure.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → p. Donor–recipient confidentiality → i.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → p. Donor–recipient confidentiality → i. (donor information critical to informed consent including donor-transmitted disease risks); PDF p. 122 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 020600 item; donor-disclosure angle distinct from DonorNet (cctc-2015), PHS consent (cctc-2023), and offer factors (cctc-2036); anchor verified on Cupples p. 122.

stem: A liver waitlist candidate with known hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has overdue surveillance testing. What re-evaluation interval is required to maintain UNOS MELD exception eligibility?

options.text: Imaging and alpha-fetoprotein testing every 3 months
Annual testing only after five years on the waitlist

explanation.rationale_correct: Patients with known HCC require imaging studies and alpha-fetoprotein testing every 3 months; this testing is required by UNOS to continue receiving MELD exception points.

rationale_incorrect.B: HCC candidates require ongoing surveillance, not one-time testing only at listing.
rationale_incorrect.C: HCC surveillance is required every 3 months, not annually after five years.
rationale_incorrect.D: Routine daily biopsy is not the UNOS HCC surveillance standard described for waitlisted candidates.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Patients with known HCC: every 3 months. Imaging studies AFP

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → 6. Liver transplant candidates → a.i. (HCC imaging and AFP every 3 months for MELD exception); PDF p. 54 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 020700 item; liver HCC surveillance angle distinct from LAS testing (cctc-2021) and pulmonary baseline (cctc-2032); anchor verified on Cupples p. 54.
